ThirtyThird Sunday in Ordinary Time Prv 311013 1920 3031 Ps 12815 1 Thes 516 Mt 251430 or 251415 1921 This weekend November 7 8 the Church celebrates the Thirtysecond Sunday in Ordinary Time Our Gospel reading reminds us of how near we are to the end of the liturgical year This is why the bridegrooms words in the parable sound so harsh to the five foolish virgins As the parable reminds us all ten were invited but it was only the indifference of the five that kept them from entering th th The closed door does not reveal a defect in the bridegrooms generosity It reveals the seriousness of being prepared for a gift we cannot demand and an hour we cannot choose Jesus ends this preaching with the command to stay awake because we do not know the day or the hour That vigilance is more than avoiding sin or keeping ourselves busy It means learning to desire the One who is coming If Jesus returned tomorrow would his coming fulfill the deepest longing of our lives or would some part of us first think of everything we had hoped to do before then There is nothing wrong with loving the life God has given us or making plans for the future But those loves should ultimately deepen our desire for him Sanctuary Stencilwork and Weekday Prayer On Monday we will welcome decorative artist Rick Fischer of Deco Illusions as he begins to prep the sanctuary for stencilwork An alumni of Bishop Dwenger High School Rick has 30 years experience as a decorative artist and an extensive list of references from churches throughout our diocese Some of his recent work includes St Joseph in Garrett Sts Peter and Paul in Huntington and the chapels at both Bishop Dwenger and Bishop Luers Rick will place scaffolding along the back wall of the sanctuary as he paints over the next three weeks He hopes to complete the stencilwork by Thanksgiving This will be the start of painting work but the majority of the remaining work will wait till the needed repairs to the woodworking is completed At this moment we are still in discussions with Shawnee Construction to schedule an appropriate time for this extensive work Throughout the week Rick will work around our weekday Mass and adoration schedule so that we can continue to use our sanctuary for our main liturgies To allow for private prayer while he is painting in the sanctuary however we will once again turn our cry room into a makeshift chapel to reserve the Blessed Sacrament throughout the week This balance will ensure that we always have space for private prayer as our renovation work continues All Saints Day and the Diocesan Synod Thank you for the warm welcome that you showed Fr Jordan DeGuire OP last weekend And a special Thank You to all of our volunteers who helped make our annual All Saints Day Party and Potluck possible I wish that I was able to be with you but I heard many wonderful comments about the fun afternoon together My time at the opening sessions of the diocesan synod were very interesting We spent two days in nearly constant listening and discussion sessions as we reviewed the five topics of the synod Catechesis Evangelization Vocations Liturgy and Outreach These sessions were very similar to the synod sessions we held here at the parish last year In three weeks we will gather again to conclude the diocesan synod We will have one final working session on an additional topic added by Bishop Rhoades Priest personnel This is tied to the topic of vocations and is meant to look at the reality of how many priests are serving in our diocese and the number of parishes to which we minister Following this last session we will then enter the voting portion of the synod This portion will last a day and half and focus on a number of proposals put together by Bishop following all of the discussions and feedback that he has received both from the individual parish sessions and this past synod session in Fort Wayne Following the voting session Bishop will then prepare his final
